implementation_notes: ConcurrentQueue<T> is the framework's answer to the hand-off problem: an unbounded MPMC FIFO built from a linked list of bounded ring buffers whose head and tail indices are kept isolated to limit false sharing - the runtime source shows an internal lock only for cross-segment transitions - so application code never writes the CAS loop. It is not strictly lock-free: cross-segment transitions take an internal lock, and the type offers no blocking take, so pair it with a SemaphoreSlim, BlockingCollection or Channel<T> when consumers must wait. Reach for System.Threading.Channels when the pipeline is async-first (bounded channels give backpressure), and hand-rolled Interlocked/Volatile code only when strict lock-freedom and fixed memory are hard requirements.
pitfalls: Count and ToArray take a consistent snapshot under an internal spin and are far more expensive than enqueue/dequeue - never use Count as the full/empty check.
There is no blocking dequeue: busy-polling TryDequeue burns a core, so wrap the queue in BlockingCollection or Channel when consumers must wait.
The BCL queue is not strictly lock-free; the cross-segment lock means a stalled thread can still delay a segment transition, so do not claim lock-free guarantees on its behalf.
